places.seoTitle: Tirathgarh Falls near Jagdalpur: Getting There, Nearby Caves
places.seoDescription: Tirathgarh Falls, 35 km from Jagdalpur in Kanger Ghati National Park: a 300-foot stepped waterfall reached by jeep from Darbha, near Kutumsar caves.

overview.text: Tirathgarh Falls lies inside Kanger Ghati National Park, about 35 km south-west of Jagdalpur in Bastar. The river spills over a stepped hillside of natural rock and drops about 300 feet,. It is one of the main sights of Bastar, which Chhattisgarh Tourism counts alongside the Chitrakot waterfall, the Kutumsar and Kailash caves, the Bastar Palace and the Bastar Dussehra festival. To get there, take the state highway from Jagdalpur towards Sukma as far as Darbha junction, then a jeep into the park; the same trip usually includes Kutumsar Caves, and the Kailash caves are also close by.

places.seoTitle: Bhoramdeo Temple: The 'Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh' near Kawardha
places.seoDescription: Bhoramdeo Temple, 18 km from Kawardha: a carved 10th–12th-century Shiva temple called the 'Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh', with Madwa Mahal nearby.

overview.text: Bhoramdeo is a group of four Shiva temples 18 km from Kawardha in Kabirdham district, set at the foot of the thickly forested Maikal hills. The main temple, built of stone, is covered with sculpture, including erotic panels in a style that recalls Khajuraho and Konark, which is why it is called the 'Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh'. The earliest temple of the group is built of brick. The complex is dated to the 10th–12th centuries, the Kalachuri period, and is credited to Naga kings. About a kilometre away stands the Madwa Mahal, or Dullhadeo, a marriage hall built in 1349 under the Naga king Ramchandra Deo, with a Shiva linga raised over 16 pillars. The Bhoramdev Wildlife Sanctuary surrounds the temple. Raipur, 134 km away, has the nearest airport and railhead.

places.seoDescription: Sirpur, 78 km east of Raipur: the 7th-century brick Lakshmana temple and excavated Buddhist viharas of an ancient Dakshina Kosala capital.

overview.text: Sirpur, a village on the Mahanadi 78 km east of Raipur, was once Shripura, a capital of the Dakshina Kosala kingdom and an important Hindu, Buddhist and Jain centre between the 5th and 12th centuries. The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang came here in the 7th century. Its best-known monument is the Lakshmana temple, dated to about 595–605 CE: a brick temple, mostly ruined, whose tall tower and finely carved sanctum doorway survive well enough to study. Excavations across the site have uncovered 12 Buddhist viharas, a Jain vihara, monolithic statues of the Buddha and Mahavira, 22 Shiva temples and 5 Vishnu temples, Shakti and Tantric shrines, an underground granary market and a 6th-century bath house.

places.seoDescription: Rajim, Gariaband district: the 7th-century Rajiv Lochan Vishnu temple with carved pillars, at the confluence of the Mahanadi and Pairy rivers.

overview.text: Rajim is a temple town in Gariaband district, near the point where the Pairy river joins the Mahanadi. Its history is the earliest recorded in the district, and its centrepiece is the Rajiv Lochan temple, an ancient shrine to Vishnu. An inscription found here, dated to the 7th century CE, records the temple's construction in the reign of King Vilasatunga, who probably belonged to a branch of the Nala dynasty. Inside, the hall is held up by twelve tall pillars carved with the faces of Hindu gods, and devotees still come from far and wide to pray to Vishnu. Rajim is also known for a statue of the Buddha seated in meditation under the Bodhi tree, carved from black stone. The town is about 30 km from Mahasamund.

places.name: Mainpat
places.summary: Chhattisgarh's 'Shimla': a plateau of Tibetan monasteries, waterfalls and the Ulta Pani gravity hill.
places.seoTitle: Mainpat: 'Shimla of Chhattisgarh', Ulta Pani, Tibetan Settlement
places.seoDescription: Mainpat hill station, 55 km from Ambikapur: Tibetan monasteries, the Ulta Pani gravity hill, Tiger Point waterfall and adventure sports.

overview.text: Mainpat is a hill station in Surguja district, in the north of Chhattisgarh, about 55 km by road from Ambikapur and 360 km from Raipur. It is popularly called the 'Shimla of Chhattisgarh'. In 1962–63 the Government of India gave land here to Tibetan refugees, and their settlement, with its Buddha temples and workshops making mats and woollen cloth, gives Mainpat a character all its own. The best-known curiosity is Ulta Pani, also called Bisar Paani, a gravity hill where water appears to flow uphill. Other sights include the Tiger Point, Fish Point and Ghaghi waterfalls, Zalzali, a patch of 'bouncing' ground, and the Parpatiya viewpoint. Visitors can also try trekking, zorbing and rappelling, and the village now has roads and rest houses for travellers.

places.name: Achanakmar Tiger Reserve
places.summary: Sal and bamboo forests of the Maikal hills, linked to Kanha, with tigers, gaur and leopards.
places.seoTitle: Achanakmar Tiger Reserve: Wildlife, Best Time to Visit
places.seoDescription: Achanakmar Tiger Reserve in the Maikal hills: 557 sq km of sal and bamboo forest with tigers, leopards and gaur; best November–June.

overview.text: Achanakmar Tiger Reserve covers the hilly sal and bamboo forests of the Maikal range in Mungeli and Gaurela Pendra Marwahi districts, around 50 km north of Mungeli, and spills over into Madhya Pradesh. It was established as a wildlife sanctuary in 1975 and declared a tiger reserve under Project Tiger in 2009, and the sanctuary covers 557.55 sq km. A forest corridor through the hills links it to Kanha Tiger Reserve, and it forms part of the Achanakmar–Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve, close to Amarkantak, the source of the Narmada and Son rivers. Its wildlife includes the Bengal tiger, leopard, gaur, chital, sambar, nilgai, sloth bear and dhole. Even a short trek, as Chhattisgarh Tourism puts it, reveals the beauty of the forest. The best season is November to June.

places.name: Tala (Devrani-Jethani Temples)
places.summary: Ancient half-ruined temples and the extraordinary Rudra Shiva statue near Bilaspur.
places.seoTitle: Tala: Devrani-Jethani Temples and the Rudra Shiva Statue
places.seoDescription: Tala near Bilaspur: the 5th–6th-century Devrani-Jethani temples at the Shivnath–Maniari confluence and a unique 7-foot Rudra Shiva statue made of animal forms.

overview.text: Tala, near the village of Ameri Kampa in Bilaspur district, sits at the confluence of the Shivnath and Maniari rivers and is often identified with the Sangamagrama of ancient Panduvamshi records. It is famous for the Devrani-Jethani temples, two half-ruined shrines that archaeologists date to the 5th or 6th century. The Devrani temple is built of red sandstone, largely in the Gupta style. Tala was discovered in 1873–74 by J. D. Welger, an assistant to the archaeologist Alexander Cunningham. Its most extraordinary find is a stone statue about 7 feet tall and weighing some 5 tonnes, whose face and body are formed from creatures and animals; historians interpret it as Rudra Shiva. It is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

items.title: Location
items.body: Near Ameri Kampa, Bilaspur district

items.title: Don't miss
items.body: Devrani temple carvings; the Rudra Shiva statue

places.name: Gangrel Dam
places.summary: Chhattisgarh's largest dam on the Mahanadi, with water sports and island views.
places.seoTitle: Gangrel Dam near Dhamtari: Water Sports, Stay, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Gangrel (Ravishankar Sagar) Dam near Dhamtari, 90 km from Raipur: Chhattisgarh's largest dam, with water sports, islands and a tourism board stay.

overview.text: Gangrel Dam, officially the Pandit Ravishankar Sagar, is built across the Mahanadi near Dhamtari, about 90 km from Raipur, and is the longest and largest dam in Chhattisgarh. Beyond irrigating farmland so that farmers can grow two crops a year and supplying water to the Bhilai Steel Plant, its reservoir has become one of the Dhamtari district's most popular outings. Chhattisgarh Tourism promotes it for water sports and its islands, and it is at its most beautiful in the monsoon, when the water is high and the islands and forest are green. The state tourism board runs a property at the dam where visitors can stay, and Onakona, on the banks of the reservoir, is another favourite spot.

places.name: Malhar
places.summary: An ancient capital near Bilaspur with restored Shiva temples and an early Vishnu sculpture.
places.seoTitle: Malhar near Bilaspur: Ancient Capital and Early Sculpture
places.seoDescription: Malhar, 30 km from Bilaspur: a 1st-millennium capital with ruined fort mounds, restored Shiva temples and a museum of early sculpture.

overview.text: Malhar, about 30 km south-east of Bilaspur in a rural setting, looks like an ordinary village today, but it was once a major city and a capital in the 1st millennium, known in inscriptions and literature as Mallar, Mallari and Sarabhapur. Its past shows in the mounds and ruins of an ancient fort, two restored Shiva temples and a museum displaying the remains of a large group of Hindu, Jain and Buddhist temples. Explorations by the Archaeological Survey of India in 1960–61 found sculpture ranging from the 2nd century BCE to the 12th century CE. The most famous find is a four-armed figure holding a conch, discus and mace, dated to about 200 BCE by a Brahmi inscription and considered one of the earliest possible representations of Vishnu in Indian sculpture.

items.body: About 30 km south-east

items.body: Restored Shiva temples, fort mounds, site museum
